authorisation_source: MIW FINAL RELEASE QUALIFICATION instruction of 8 September 2026, section 4 (BULK JUPITER - SPECIAL RELEASE CHECK), which directs that if either flagged card carries a live material factual error it is to be classified RELEASE_BLOCKING_P1 and given a bounded surgical correction, expressly notwithstanding that it sat outside Pass-2 terminal scope. Pass 2 is not reopened by this record and no discovery tranche was run: the two cards were named in the instruction and only those two cards were opened.
authority: PRIMARY, read at source. Bahamas Maritime Authority, 'M.v Bulk Jupiter - Marine Safety Investigation Report', published 18 August 2015 - the flag State's own report, 64 pages. Section 4.2: the vessel 'foundered ... within approximately 20 minutes', and separately the window from the 0640 general alarm to the 0700 EPIRB transmission 'was unlikely to be more than 20 minutes'. Sections 4.3.12-4.3.13 and 5.1: an average moisture content of 21.3% across 46,400t loaded over thirteen days, against 10% declared on all three declarations. Section 5.1: 'there is no physical evidence to confirm what caused the vessel to adopt an unrecoverable list to starboard and subsequent capsize', and the report concludes only that it is 'most probable that either liquefaction or a free surface effect induced an unrecoverable list'. Sections 3.12-3.18 and 4.5: NE monsoon, forecast Beaufort 6-7, sea state 4-6, average wave height 2.2m - which is why QB5_A's 'heavy weather' was tested and KEPT rather than removed on suspicion. SUPPORTING, already held in this repository at P1: CCC.1/Circ.2 of 20 October 2015, read at source for QP2509-Q1, which records that CCC 2 considered the BAHAMAS submission on the loss - the IMO's role was to receive that submission and circulate the warning, not to investigate. The flag-State duty is SOLAS XI-1/6 with the Casualty Investigation Code (MSC.255(84)), which this corpus already teaches and which CORR-GPT-PASS3 corrected to the Code's own term, 'marine safety investigation' - the term the BMA report itself uses in its title.
title: QB8_A q4 - the Bulk Jupiter Casualty Link attributed the marine safety investigation to the IMO, and stated an expressly qualified finding as a conclusion.
candidate_claim: Not a candidate report. Raised by the final release qualification's section 4, which required the card to be read against source rather than accepted at the severity the terminal report had assigned it.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD, and more seriously than the P2/P3 the terminal report carried. Attributing a casualty investigation to the IMO is not a citation slip: who investigates a marine casualty is itself examinable at MEO Class I, so the card taught a wrong answer to a question the candidate will be asked directly, and it did so in a Casualty Link block, which is memorisation-weighted by design.

propagation.same_defect_swept: 'investigation by the IMO', and the wider pattern of attributing a casualty investigation or inquiry to the IMO, were searched across every HTML page under meoclass1/. Exactly one site exists corpus-wide: QB8_A#q4, corrected here.
propagation.same_family_prior: None. This is the first correction in the 'a casualty was investigated by the IMO' class, recorded as known trap 131.
propagation.corpus_agreement_checked: The four other Bulk Jupiter sites were read for contradiction with the corrected text. QB10_B#q1 (2 January 2015, off Vung Tau, 18 of 19 crew lost, bauxite liquefaction not a cargo shift, average cargo moisture 21.3%), QB8_H#q5, QB2_B_CheatSheet and the QP2304 / QP2509 past-paper layer all agree with the corrected wording and are byte-identical after this record.
propagation.not_swept_reported: The past-paper layer (QP2304, QP2501, QP2509) characterises the Bulk Jupiter mechanism as DYNAMIC SEPARATION and says expressly that it is not a simple liquefaction case, while the QB layer says liquefaction. That divergence is real and is NOT closed here. Both corrected cards now state the mechanism as the flag State's report states it, which is the narrower and safer claim, and the nuance is REPORTED as post-release hardening rather than swept - section 15 of the release instruction requires a new class to be reported rather than expanded.
propagation.derived_surfaces: qb_content_index.json and qb_content_index_governed.json regenerate to no-ops on the corrected page; corpus 761 / 86 unchanged; no q-text and no card identity was touched, so no index, examiner, topic or search surface moves.

invariants: The card's q-text is unchanged, so no anchor, no identity and no derived surface moves. Corpus stays 761 / 86.
The Group C framing, the fines-and-moisture mechanism and the IMSBC individual-schedule revision are all preserved; only the attribution, the certainty and the particulars changed.
The 18-of-19 crew toll is now stated where the card had 'the loss of 18 crew members' without the denominator.
The card's Examiner Chain, its IMSBC group teaching and every other block on it are byte-identical.
No other card, cheat sheet, notes page or past paper was edited by this record.

cards.what_changed: Casualty Link. 'The subsequent investigation by the IMO concluded that ... the material underwent rapid liquefaction (Group A transition), causing an immediate loss of stability and a sudden capsize' replaced. The investigating body is now named as the Bahamas Maritime Authority acting as flag State, with the flag-State duty cited (SOLAS XI-1/6 and the Casualty Investigation Code) and the IMO's actual role stated - it received the Bahamas submission and issued the warning. The finding is now stated at the strength the report states it: no physical evidence of cause, and only a most-probable finding of liquefaction OR a free-surface effect. Particulars corrected or added from the same report: the date (2 January 2015), the position (South China Sea off Vung Tau), the tonnage (46,400t, was 46,000t), the crew toll with its denominator (18 of 19) and the foundering time (approximately 20 minutes, was 'sank rapidly'). The 21.3%-against-10%-declared moisture pair added, which is the number this card exists to make memorable and which QB10_B already carried. The IMSBC tail now names the separate Group A BAUXITE FINES schedule the revision produced.
